name: Sunken Dig Site
summary: In the arid canyon of Thousand Needles, the excavation known across later eras as the Sunken Dig Site is currently the dry, silithid-infested Rustmaul Dig Site. Adventurers who explore the canyon floor find an active prospecting ground overrun by alien insectoids rather than floodwaters. Any notion of flooded shafts belongs strictly to tales of distant, speculative futures.

sections.title: A Dry and Infested Excavation
sections.body: Before any great deluge altered southern Kalimdor, the southern canyons of Thousand Needles remained baking, dust-choked stone. Here, dwarven prospectors sought subterranean minerals and Titan remnants, only to disturb the ravenous silithid lurking beneath the earth. The site was rapidly overrun by insectoid horrors, transforming the dig shafts and nearby rock outcroppings into a lethal hive colony rather than an underwater curiosity.

sections.title: Prospects Cut Short
sections.body: While later rumors speak of gnomish ice cream operations and submerged wreckage, the harsh present reality in year 25 ADP is much more grounded. The area remains known as the Rustmaul Dig Site, an active danger zone where surface miners struggle against aggressive burrowers and chitinous hunters that threaten anyone traversing the southern passes toward Tanaris.

faq.q: Is the Sunken Dig Site flooded right now?
faq.answer: No. In the present era of 25 ADP, Thousand Needles is entirely dry rock, salt flats, and canyon floor. The flooded Sunken Dig Site exists only in accounts of possible cataclysms yet to come; right now, it is the dry, bug-infested Rustmaul Dig Site.

faq.q: What is the site called in this era?
faq.answer: Currently, travelers know this excavation as the Rustmaul Dig Site. It was an ambitious prospecting venture that met a violent end when the workers dug straight into a silithid hive.

faq.q: Who occupies the dig site currently?
faq.answer: The excavation is completely overrun by the silithid—chitinous, insectoid predators that tunnel under Kalimdor. Any miners who originally worked the claims were either killed or driven off.

faq.q: Where is the gnome Brivelthwerp and his ice cream boat?
faq.answer: Brivelthwerp and his tugboat are not here. Without a massive body of water filling the canyon, there is nowhere for a boat to float, and his ill-fated refrigeration venture has not taken place.

angles.text: The abandoned tools and exposed stone around the excavation are tempting, but the silithid infestation makes prospecting here suicidal for all but the most heavily armed miners.
Dwarven excavation teams pushed deep into the canyon floor seeking archaeological riches, only to discover that unearthing ancient horrors is an occupational hazard in Kalimdor.
